verdict.rationale: BigQuery documents several first-party programmatic surfaces: the bq CLI for creating datasets, loading data and querying tables, the Storage Write API, ODBC/JDBC drivers that let you 'use BigQuery features' from your own tooling, and SDKs such as Rust (Preview). Nothing in the evidence claims or shows that every UI capability is reachable through the API, and UI features like data canvas, conversational analytics and data insights are only described as console experiences. missing for 10: an explicit API-parity statement or REST API reference covering all console features, evidence that UI-centric features (data canvas, conversational analytics, data insights, notebooks) are API-accessible, independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: learn how to use bq, the Python-based command-line interface (CLI) tool for BigQuery to create a dataset, load sample data, and query tables
connect your applications to BigQuery, letting you use BigQuery features with your preferred tooling and infrastructure
The Rust SDK for BigQuery is now in Preview.
The Storage Write API (gRPC) has lower pricing and more robust features, including exactly-once delivery semantics.
